timeline.tweet: I've just seen what's happened in Japan with severe storms and landslides. I am so sorry to hear people have lost their lives due to this and hope that those families effected and Japan can recover.

On this day in 2015 Satoru Iwata sadly passed away. His contributions to the video game industry helped shape who I am and I will always be grateful for the wonderful experiences I have gained because of him. Thank you Iwata. You will always be remembered and loved.

I'll bite 😄 #4 for me, so what is my religion? Well I'd be an agnostic atheist. I don't believe there is a god or higher power and trust scientific methods and fact. However, if there were any evidence put forward to suggest that there is a higher power I'd be open to it.

I got to meet up with my Year 11 and 12 Psychology teacher today for the first time in five years and was able to finally thank him for fostering a love for Psychology and Teaching that made me who I am today. If there’s a teacher like that for you please let them know!

It's part of an ongoing trend around the world at the moment. Tensions are getting high, everything is becoming partisan and there is an abundant focus on all things controversial and negative. I wish everyone could realise we're all human and just get along.

Whilst I'm glad to see that the official statement from our PM does in fact call the events of today out as what they are, terrorism, I am sickened and saddened to see significant members of Australia demonstrate the racist and dangerous attitudes that do exist in our country.

This coming week is National Reconciliation Week. Building positive relationships between Aboriginal and Torres Straight Islander people and other Australians is such an important thing to do. We need to move forward on a foundation of truth. #NRW2019

The climate protests occurring across Australia today should be welcomed and listened to. The idea that "the classroom is being politicised" when students are involved in these demonstrations is ridiculous. You can not expect the classroom to ignore the world around it!

I had no desire for achieving anything, and, although I never had thoughts of self-harm or suicide, I really did not have any desire to engage with my life happening around me. I stopped playing guitar, didn't even pick up a book, and for a good year I was dulled. (4/11)
It finally came through today! As of the 17th of January 2019 I am provisionally registered as a teacher in Victoria! I cannot wait for what awaits me as a teacher!

This is a big moment for Aboriginal rights in Australia. Like Mabo this will provide further legal standing and precedent for Aboriginal rights moving forward. The decision being split 4-3 is a damning display of the racist views still present in Australia, however...

Today is National Sorry Day. It is important that we acknowledge the inhuman treatment of Indigenous people’s during the Stolen Generation and recognise the fact that, due to inter-generational trauma, it is still affecting people today. I know this, and I am sorry.

The protests happening in the US are a horrifying glimpse at the racist core of the country. Sadly this is also true for Australia. Indigenous peoples are disproportionately incarcerated and mistreated by the police in our country and it is heartbreaking. #blacklivesmatter
We had a discussion with my History class today about how scary the similarities actually are with the current administration and the rise of the Nazi party. Much too similar for my liking.

The premier has made the hard call, and full respect for it. 6 weeks hard lockdown is exactly what we need to do. Here’s hoping this’ll be what it takes to really knock this virus out from the community.

Watching #FightForPlanetA. There are significant areas contributing to energy consumption just from households alone! Not just that, multinational companies are also clearly skirting their responsibilities and the government is complicit. This is the issue of my generation!

Two massive fires. Two different countries. Having lived through and experienced the bushfires in Australia I can imagine the fear and panic that people in the US may be feeling. #ClimateChange is the greatest threat to our world and these fires are a sign that it is worsening.
